entities.summary: Critolaus (b. 199 BCE, Phaselis) was a philosopher or thinker of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in Phaselis. Known in the fields of philosophers & thinkers.\ \ He was influenced by various Hellenistic and Stoic philosophers, including Zeno of Citium and Cleanthes of Assos, and his own ideas were likely shaped by his involvement with the Stoic school.\ \ Critolaus' philosophical contributions were primarily focused on the nature of reality, the ideal of human virtue, and the concept of the universe's underlying structure. His work, though not widely recognized during his lifetime, has had a lasting impact on Western philosophy.\ \ Critolaus' significance can be seen in the broader context of Classical Greek thought, which laid the groundwork for many subsequent philosophical movements. His emphasis on reason, self-control, and indifference to external events aligns with the Stoic ideals of the time.
